questions.questionText: What does regularization add to a model's cost function?
options: A penalty for large weight values, discouraging the model from relying too heavily on any one feature
A bonus for using more features
A penalty for using too little training data
A term that speeds up gradient descent
questions.correctAnswer: A penalty for large weight values, discouraging the model from relying too heavily on any one feature
questions.explanation: Regularization directly penalizes weight magnitude in the cost function, trading a little training fit for smaller, more stable weights that generalize better.

questions.questionText: What's the key practical difference between L1 (Lasso) and L2 (Ridge) regularization?
options: L1 tends to push irrelevant weights to exactly zero (feature selection); L2 shrinks weights smoothly but rarely to exactly zero
L2 always performs better than L1
L1 can only be used with decision trees
questions.correctAnswer: L1 tends to push irrelevant weights to exactly zero (feature selection); L2 shrinks weights smoothly but rarely to exactly zero
questions.explanation: L1's absolute-value penalty has a geometry that tends to zero out weights entirely, effectively performing automatic feature selection, while L2's squared penalty shrinks weights smoothly without eliminating them.

questions.questionText: What happens if the regularization strength (lambda / alpha) is set far too high?
options: The model perfectly fits the training data
The penalty dominates the loss, pushing weights toward zero regardless of the data — the model underfits
Regularization strength has no effect on model behavior
The model automatically switches from L1 to L2
questions.correctAnswer: The penalty dominates the loss, pushing weights toward zero regardless of the data — the model underfits
questions.explanation: Too much regularization overwhelms the actual data-fitting term, forcing weights toward zero even when the data supports larger values — the same underfitting failure mode as an overly simple model.
